context:
Use this small collection of 10 papers, written out in full; it is the entire dataset. The vocabulary has exactly four concepts: parsing, tagging, summarization, speech recognition. Papers:
- edge.1 (2020; concepts: parsing): We study parsing of the corpus with a chart-parser. The parser builds trees, and each tree is scored by a grammar over a lattice.
- edge.2 (2020; concepts: parsing): Parsing errors in the corpus: a parser misreads 2020 trees, so we add a grammar and a lattice to it. Is it of an ab xy help?
- edge.3 (2020; concepts: tagging): Tagging the corpus with tags from a lexicon; we tag 100 sentences of the corpus.
- edge.4 (2020; concepts: tagging): A tagging model labels every word in the corpus, and the lexicon lists each word.
- edge.5 (2021; concepts: parsing): Parsing the corpus again: the parser reads trees with a shift-reduce chart and an oracle.
- edge.6 (2021; concepts: tagging): Tagging with an oracle: the tagger labels the corpus, and the model reads a lexicon.
- edge.7 (2021; concepts: tagging): Tagging speech in the corpus: a tagger reads transcripts and labels words.
- edge.8 (2021; concepts: summarization): Summarization of the corpus: a model writes summaries of each document.
- edge.9 (2021; concepts: summarization): Summarization models compress documents in the corpus into short summaries.
- edge.10 (2021; concepts: none): The corpus holds documents and transcripts, and a model reads them.

Topic selection: the papers published from first_year through last_year inclusive whose concepts include the given concept. The whole collection is all 10 papers.

Tokenize each abstract exactly by these rules: Unicode NFKC normalize, lowercase, replace every character outside a-z or 0-9 by a space, split on whitespace; for each token longer than 3 characters that ends in s but not ss, us or is, remove that final s (so misreads becomes misread, and reads becomes read). A term is a resulting token of at least 3 characters that is not all digits and not in the stopword list below.

Stopword list (already in this normalized form): about, above, across, after, again, against, all, almost, alone, along, already, also, although, alway, among, and, another, any, anyone, anything, are, around, because, been, before, being, below, beside, between, both, but, can, cannot, could, did, doe, doing, done, down, during, each, either, else, enough, etc, even, ever, every, few, for, from, further, had, hardly, has, have, having, her, here, herself, him, himself, his, how, however, into, its, itself, just, least, less, like, many, may, might, more, most, mostly, much, must, myself, near, neither, never, nevertheless, none, nor, not, now, off, often, once, one, only, onto, other, otherwise, our, ourselve, out, over, own, per, perhap, quite, rather, same, several, shall, she, should, since, some, such, than, that, the, their, them, themselve, then, there, therefore, these, they, this, those, though, through, throughout, thus, too, toward, under, unless, until, upon, very, via, was, well, were, what, whatever, when, whenever, where, wherea, whether, which, while, who, whom, whose, why, will, with, within, without, would, yet, you, your, yourself, yourselve.

Scoring and ranking: for each distinct term of the selected abstracts, tf is the total number of occurrences in those abstracts; its document frequency df is the number of papers among all 10 whose abstract contains the term at least once; N in the score is 10, the whole collection, not the selected count. score = tf times ln(N / df). Rank all terms by score descending; when scores tie, by term alphabetically ascending. The papers output is the number of selected papers. The terms output is the first k terms of that ranking, or all ranked terms if there are fewer than k. If no paper is selected, terms is empty and papers is 0.
